approach: Add athena-core module `records_import` with `import_records(git, c0) -> Result<String, ImportError>`. It lists records/ at C0 with Git::ls_tree, reads each blob with cat_blob, and builds an ImportManifest (RecordId::generate(crate::now()), athena_data::sha256_hex for hashes). It refuses if RecordsWriter::tip() is Some. It then does one RecordsWriter::append of a Change::put per file plus import-manifest.json, and calls a public `verify_import(git, c0, commit)` that re-reads the new commit and compares it with C0. The checks, in order: manifest parses as HistoryRecord::ImportManifest and validates; every non-manifest tree file against C0 for Missing, Extra, BlobMismatch and HashMismatch (sha256 of the bytes against the manifest); then counts for the tree and the manifest against C0. Each failure is its own ImportError variant. Tests run on scratch repositories. The doc-only edits to athena-git, the design doc and the CHANGELOG say the importer exists and is not wired in.

decisions.choice: Put the importer in athena-core and use athena_data::sha256_hex for hashing.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-git and athena-data. sha256_hex is already exported and used in proposals.rs, so no new hashing dependency is needed. The only new dependency is thiserror (workspace 2) for the error enum.

rejected.why: It duplicates sha256_hex and adds a dependency for nothing.

decisions.choice: Refuse a second import by checking RecordsWriter::tip() is None before writing. Return ImportError::AlreadyImported without touching the branch.
decisions.reason: The writer's same-bytes no-op would make a repeat import look like success (the new manifest id differs, so it would be refused only by accident). An explicit check gives a clear error and the tip stays unchanged. A race is still safe: the first write uses the all-zero expected id, so the compare-and-swap rejects a concurrent branch creation.

rejected.why: It would not be a distinct, deliberate error. Because the generated id differs each run, the manifest put would be refused as a changed file, which is accidental.

decisions.choice: Keep a private `import_with(git, c0, tamper)` hook that lets tests alter the change list before writing. `verify_import` is public and always runs on the committed tree.
decisions.reason: Tests can then produce a really-committed bad commit (file dropped, bytes changed, extra file, duplicated manifest entry). The self-check is exercised against real commits without hand-built git plumbing.

rejected.option: Craft bad commits with git checkout/commit in the work tree
rejected.why: It is more fragile and slower. It also needs manifest tampering by hand.

decisions.choice: Refuse any records/ entry that is not a regular 100644 blob, and refuse an empty records/ at C0.
decisions.reason: The writer always writes mode 100644, so a symlink or executable would silently differ. An empty import must not count as success (no-empty-success). Both get their own error variant.

rejected.option: Copy modes or skip the odd entries
rejected.why: The writer cannot store other modes, and skipping would make the self-check misleading.

decisions.choice: Edit athena-git lib.rs and records_branch.rs as doc comments only, replacing 'Nothing calls this writer yet' with a pointer to the importer. Change no code.
decisions.reason: Both files are listed as deliverables. The stale statement would otherwise be wrong once the importer uses the writer.

rejected.why: athena-core tests can build their own scratch repo with Git::isolated, as chain.rs does, so no API change is needed.

steps: Add thiserror.workspace to crates/athena-core/Cargo.toml and let cargo update Cargo.lock (cargo build --locked will fail until it is updated, so run cargo build once).

Create records_import.rs. Module docs cover: the purpose; the steps; the self-check; append-only, so a second import is refused; and the note that it is not wired into the pipeline, the CLI or CI and has not been run against main (job 7 will do that).

Write ImportError (thiserror) with variants: Git(GitError) and Records(RecordsError) transparent, AlreadyImported{tip}, EmptyRecords{c0}, UnsupportedEntry{path,mode}, ManifestMissing, ManifestInvalid(String), Missing{path}, Extra{path}, BlobMismatch{path,expected,found}, HashMismatch{path}, CountMismatch{expected,found,what}.

Write import_records(git,&str c0) -> Result<String,ImportError>. It calls import_with(git,c0,|_|{}). import_with does: resolve c0 and fail if it is not a commit; check writer.tip() is None; ls_tree(c0) filtered to paths starting 'records/', refusing non-blob or non-100644 entries; refuse if empty; cat_blob each file; build the ImportManifest (c0 full sha, entries sorted by path, sha256_hex); validate it; serialize with serde_json::to_vec_pretty over HistoryRecord::ImportManifest; apply the tamper hook to the Vec<Change>; RecordsWriter::append once; then verify_import. Decide what to do if verification fails: return the error, and the commit stays on the branch because the branch is append-only (say so in the docs).

Write pub verify_import(git,c0,commit). Re-list C0's records/ files. Read import-manifest.json from the commit with show_file, parse it with HistoryRecord::parse, and require the ImportManifest variant with c0 equal. List the commit's tree. Compare files other than the manifest path against C0 in this order: Missing, Extra, BlobMismatch. Read each blob and compare its sha256_hex to the manifest entry (HashMismatch). Compare manifest entries against C0 (blob ids, sha256). Compare the tree count and the manifest count to C0's count (CountMismatch).

Write tests with a local repo() helper like chain.rs's (Git::isolated, init -b main, write files, add, commit): full import; manifest content; missing, changed, extra, count-mismatch and manifest-hash cases using the hook; a control; second import refused with the tip unchanged; empty records/ refused; a non-blob entry (a symlink) refused; an import that leaves main and the work tree untouched.
Update the doc comments in records_branch.rs (and lib.rs if stale text exists), the design doc and the CHANGELOG.
Run cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, and cargo test --workspace --locked.

risks.risk: Test-only tamper hook leaks into production behavior.
risks.mitigation: The hook is a closure parameter of a private fn. The public import_records passes a no-op, and the self-check always runs on the committed tree.

risks.risk: A bad import leaves a commit on the append-only branch that cannot be removed.
risks.mitigation: This is by design for the append-only branch. Document it. The failure is loud, and the real run is out of scope here (job 7 runs it after a scratch run).

risks.risk: Scratch repos need git identity or signing config.
risks.mitigation: Use Git::isolated as the existing tests do. The writer reads signs_commits from the isolated config.
records/ files are small JSON/text. Note the assumption in the docs.
Run cargo build once to update Cargo.lock and commit the result. thiserror is already in the lockfile.

demonstrations.method: Test `full_import_passes_self_check_and_copies_every_file`. It builds a scratch repo whose C0 has several nested files under records/ (including a non-UTF-8 binary file), plus a file outside records/. It calls import_records, then lists the new commit with ls_tree.
demonstrations.observes: import_records returns Ok. athena/records points at the returned commit. The tree holds exactly the records/ paths with blob ids equal to C0's, plus import-manifest.json, and nothing from outside records/.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the copy or the self-check were missing or wrong, the tree listing or blob-id assertions would fail, or the import would return an error.

demonstrations.method: Test `manifest_lists_each_path_with_blob_and_sha256`. It reads import-manifest.json from the new commit and parses it with HistoryRecord::parse. It checks the variant is ImportManifest and that validate() is Ok. It compares the entries with C0's ls_tree output and an independent sha256_hex of each file's bytes.
demonstrations.observes: The manifest c0 equals the C0 id. The entry count equals the number of records/ files at C0. Each entry's path and blob_id match C0, and each sha256 matches the content hash.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the manifest were missing an entry or carried wrong hashes or blob ids, the equality assertions would fail.

demonstrations.method: Tests `self_check_fails_on_missing_file`, `..._changed_file`, `..._extra_file`, `..._count_mismatch` (plus a manifest-hash-mismatch case). Each uses the import_with tamper hook to commit a bad import on a fresh scratch repo, then asserts the specific ImportError variant. A control test asserts the untampered import is Ok.
demonstrations.observes: The variants are Missing{path}, BlobMismatch/HashMismatch{path}, Extra{path} and CountMismatch{..}, each distinct, using matches!. The control import passes, so the failures come from the tampering.
demonstrations.fails_without: A self-check that only compared counts, or that was skipped, would return Ok or the wrong variant for at least one tampering case.

demonstrations.method: Test `second_import_is_refused_and_tip_unchanged`. It imports once and records the tip. It imports again into the same repo and asserts AlreadyImported, then asserts the tip and the commit count are unchanged. A second test shows an unrelated pre-existing athena/records branch also blocks the import.
demonstrations.observes: The second call returns ImportError::AlreadyImported. rev-parse of athena/records is identical before and after, and the rev-list count is 1.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the tip check, the second call would either add a commit or fail with a different writer error, and the variant or tip assertion would fail.

demonstrations.observes: The diff lists only the deliverable files, with no athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows or CLI file. Grep for `records_import` and `import_records` shows hits only in records_import.rs, lib.rs (the `pub mod` line), the docs and the CHANGELOG. The module //! text says it is not wired into the pipeline, the CLI or CI, and has not been run against main.

demonstrations.method: Run the full gates. Review confirms the module calls RecordsWriter::append and ImportManifest, with no copy of the writer's logic.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean. A grep of records_import.rs shows RecordsWriter and ImportManifest in use, and no update-ref, commit_tree or hash-object calls.
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile error, a failing test, a clippy warning or a formatting diff would fail the respective command.
